solution: Let \(\sqrt{-8-6i} = a+bi\). Squaring, \(a^2-b^2 = -8\) and \(2ab = -6\). Also \(a^2+b^2 = |-8-6i| = \sqrt{64+36} = 10\). Adding gives \(2a^2 = 2\), so \(a = \pm 1\); subtracting gives \(2b^2 = 18\), so \(b = \pm 3\). Since \(ab = -3 < 0\), \(a\) and \(b\) carry opposite signs. \(\therefore \sqrt{-8-6i} = \pm(1-3i)\)

Let \(\sqrt{7+24i} = a+bi\). Squaring, \(a^2-b^2 = 7\) and \(2ab = 24\). Also \(a^2+b^2 = \sqrt{49+576} = 25\). Hence \(a^2 = 16\) and \(b^2 = 9\), so \(a = \pm 4\), \(b = \pm 3\). Since \(ab = 12 > 0\), \(a\) and \(b\) carry the same sign. \(\therefore \sqrt{7+24i} = \pm(4+3i)\)

Let \(\sqrt{1+4\sqrt{3}\,i} = a+bi\). Squaring, \(a^2-b^2 = 1\) and \(2ab = 4\sqrt{3}\). Also \(a^2+b^2 = \sqrt{1+48} = 7\). Hence \(a^2 = 4\) and \(b^2 = 3\), so \(a = \pm 2\), \(b = \pm\sqrt{3}\). Since \(ab = 2\sqrt{3} > 0\), \(a\) and \(b\) carry the same sign, and indeed \((2+\sqrt{3}\,i)^2 = 4 + 4\sqrt{3}\,i - 3 = 1 + 4\sqrt{3}\,i\). \(\therefore \sqrt{1+4\sqrt{3}\,i} = \pm(2+\sqrt{3}\,i)\)

But \((2-\sqrt{3}\,i)^2 = 4 - 4\sqrt{3}\,i - 3 = 1 - 4\sqrt{3}\,i\), the CONJUGATE of the given number, so the sign of the imaginary part in the key is wrong. The stem was checked against the printed page and does read \(1+4\sqrt{3}\,i\).]

solution: Let \(\sqrt{3+2\sqrt{10}\,i} = a+bi\). Squaring, \(a^2-b^2 = 3\) and \(2ab = 2\sqrt{10}\). Also \(a^2+b^2 = \sqrt{9+40} = 7\). Hence \(a^2 = 5\) and \(b^2 = 2\), so \(a = \pm\sqrt{5}\), \(b = \pm\sqrt{2}\). Since \(ab = \sqrt{10} > 0\), \(a\) and \(b\) carry the same sign. \(\therefore \sqrt{3+2\sqrt{10}\,i} = \pm(\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}\,i)\)

Here \(2(1-\sqrt{3}\,i) = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i\). Let \(\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{3}\,i} = a+bi\), so \(a^2-b^2 = 2\) and \(2ab = -2\sqrt{3}\). Also \(a^2+b^2 = \sqrt{4+12} = 4\). Hence \(a^2 = 3\) and \(b^2 = 1\), so \(a = \pm\sqrt{3}\), \(b = \pm 1\). Since \(ab = -\sqrt{3} < 0\), \(a\) and \(b\) carry opposite signs. \(\therefore \sqrt{2(1-\sqrt{3}\,i)} = \pm(\sqrt{3}-i)\)

solution: Here \(a = 2\), \(b = -\sqrt{3}\), \(c = 1\), so \(b^2-4ac = 3 - 8 = -5\). Then \(x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{-5}}{4}\). \(\therefore x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{5}\,i}{4}\) or \(x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{5}\,i}{4}\)
Here the discriminant is \((3i)^2 - 4(1)(10) = -9 - 40 = -49\), and \(\sqrt{-49} = 7i\). Then \(x = \dfrac{-3i \pm 7i}{2}\). \(\therefore x = 2i\) or \(x = -5i\)
Here the discriminant is \((3i)^2 - 4(2)(2) = -9 - 16 = -25\), and \(\sqrt{-25} = 5i\). Then \(x = \dfrac{-3i \pm 5i}{4}\). \(\therefore x = \dfrac{i}{2}\) or \(x = -2i\)
Here the discriminant is \((4i)^2 - 4(1)(-4) = -16 + 16 = 0\), so the roots are equal. \(x = \dfrac{-4i}{2}\). (Equivalently \(x^2+4ix-4 = (x+2i)^2\).) \(\therefore x = -2i\) (a repeated root)

Multiplying \(ix^2-4x-4i = 0\) throughout by \(-i\) gives \(x^2 + 4ix - 4 = 0\). Its discriminant is \((4i)^2 + 16 = -16 + 16 = 0\), so \(x = \dfrac{-4i}{2}\). \(\therefore x = -2i\) (a repeated root)
The sum of the roots is \(3\sqrt{2}+2i\) and their product is \(6\sqrt{2}\,i = (3\sqrt{2})(2i)\), so the equation factorises as \((x-3\sqrt{2})(x-2i) = 0\). \(\therefore x = 3\sqrt{2}\) or \(x = 2i\)

The discriminant is \((5-i)^2 - 4(2+i)\cdot 2(1-i) = (24-10i) - 8(3-i) = (24-10i) - (24-8i) = -2i\). Now \(\sqrt{-2i} = \pm(1-i)\), since \((1-i)^2 = -2i\). So \(x = \dfrac{(5-i) \pm (1-i)}{2(2+i)}\). Taking the plus sign, \(x = \dfrac{6-2i}{4+2i} = \dfrac{3-i}{2+i} = \dfrac{(3-i)(2-i)}{5} = \dfrac{5-5i}{5} = 1-i\). Taking the minus sign, \(x = \dfrac{4}{4+2i} = \dfrac{2}{2+i} = \dfrac{2(2-i)}{5} = \dfrac{4-2i}{5}\). \(\therefore x = 1-i\) or \(x = \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{2}{5}i\)

Since \(x = 2+3i\), \(x-2 = 3i\), and squaring gives \(x^2-4x+4 = -9\), i.e. \(x^2-4x+13 = 0\). Dividing, \(x^3-x^2+x+46 = (x^2-4x+13)(x+3) + 7\). The first term vanishes at \(x = 2+3i\). \(\therefore x^3-x^2+x+46 = 7\)

First \(x = \dfrac{25}{3-4i} = \dfrac{25(3+4i)}{9+16} = 3+4i\). Then \(x-3 = 4i\), and squaring gives \(x^2-6x+9 = -16\), i.e. \(x^2-6x+25 = 0\). Dividing, \(2x^3-11x^2+44x+27 = (x^2-6x+25)(2x+1) + 2\), and the first term vanishes. \(\therefore 2x^3-11x^2+44x+27 = 2\)

First \(x = \dfrac{5}{1-2i} = \dfrac{5(1+2i)}{1+4} = 1+2i\). Then \(x-1 = 2i\), and squaring gives \(x^2-2x+1 = -4\), i.e. \(x^2-2x+5 = 0\). Dividing, \(x^3+x^2-x+22 = (x^2-2x+5)(x+3) + 7\), and the first term vanishes. \(\therefore x^3+x^2-x+22 = 7\)

Here \(x = -2-\sqrt{3}\,i\), so \(x+2 = -\sqrt{3}\,i\), and squaring gives \(x^2+4x+4 = -3\), i.e. \(x^2+4x+7 = 0\). Dividing, \(2x^4+5x^3+7x^2-x+41 = (x^2+4x+7)(2x^2-3x+5) + 6\), and the first term vanishes. \(\therefore 2x^4+5x^3+7x^2-x+41 = 6\)
